title: Quantum Circuit for General Unitary: Improved T-count via Block Flattening and Dilation
authors: Pei Yuan, Shengyu Zhang, Wei Zi
abstract: Synthesizing arbitrary $n$-qubit unitaries using as few non-Clifford gates as possible is a central problem in fault-tolerant quantum compilation. We present a Clifford+$T$ quantum circuit construction that approximately implements any classically specified unitary to within error $ε$ and achieves a worst-case $T$-count with leading exponential scaling of $2^{5n/4}$ whenever $\log(1/ε)=\operatorname{poly}(n)$. This improves upon the best previous $2^{4n/3}$ scaling. The key innovation lies in treating the target unitary as a single block-encoded object rather than a long product of simpler operations. A technique of block flattening controls the normalization while preserving an efficient implementation of the block encoding; subsequently, quantum singular value transformation maps its common singular value to one, thereby recovering the target unitary.
summary: This paper presents an improved method for compiling general unitary quantum circuits into the resource-constrained Clifford+T model. By employing block flattening and Quantum Singular Value Transformation, the authors reduce the worst-case T-gate count scaling from $O(2^{4n/3})$ to $O(2^{5n/4})$. This advancement is crucial for making large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation more resource-efficient.
main_problem: The central problem is synthesizing arbitrary n-qubit unitaries using the minimum possible number of non-Clifford gates (T-count) for fault-tolerant quantum compilation.
main_result: The authors achieve a worst-case T-count scaling of O(2^(5n/4)), improving upon previous bounds of O(2^(4n/3)).
method: The technique involves treating the target unitary as a block-encoded object, which is then flattened using block flattening and recovered via Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT).
model_or_system: The model is quantum computation implemented by unitary transformations U in the Clifford+T circuit model, acting on n qubits.
key_observables: T-count (the primary cost measure), approximation error (ε), and the exponential scaling of the T-count.
important_parameters: n (number of qubits), ε (approximation error), and the scaling exponents (e.g., 5/4).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the error $\log(1/\epsilon)$ is polynomial in $n$, and that classical pre-processing time is excluded from the quantum resource count.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for efficient unitary synthesis, then detailing the block flattening technique using Walsh transforms, followed by the block encoding via Julia-Halmos dilation, and finally applying QSVT to achieve the improved T-count bounds.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the resource overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computation, which is critical for realizing large-scale quantum processors.
